contents.html: Abstract
contents.html_ja: 概要

contents.html: Hash functions that compute a fixed-length message digest from arbitrary length messages are widely used for many purposes in information security. This document provides security guidelines for achieving the required or desired security strengths when using cryptographic applications that employ the approved hash functions specified in Federal Information Processing Standard (FIPS) 180-4. These include functions such as digital signatures, Keyed-hash Message Authentication Codes (HMACs) and Hash-based Key Derivation Functions (Hash-based KDFs).
contents.html_ja: 任意の長さのメッセージから固定長のメッセージダイジェストを計算するハッシュ関数は、情報セキュリティの多くの用途で広く使用されている。本書は、連邦情報処理標準（FIPS）180-4で規定される承認済みハッシュ関数を用いる暗号アプリケーションにおいて、要求される、または望ましいセキュリティ強度を実現するためのセキュリティ指針を示す。対象には、デジタル署名、鍵付きハッシュメッセージ認証コード（HMAC）、ハッシュベース鍵導出関数（ハッシュベースKDF）などが含まれる。

contents.html: KEY WORDS: digital signatures, hash algorithm, hash function, hash-based key derivation algorithms, hash value, HMAC, message digest, randomized hashing, random number generation, SHA, truncated hash values.
contents.html_ja: キーワード：デジタル署名、ハッシュアルゴリズム、ハッシュ関数、ハッシュベース鍵導出アルゴリズム、ハッシュ値、HMAC、メッセージダイジェスト、ランダム化ハッシュ、乱数生成、SHA、切り詰められたハッシュ値。

contents.html: 1 Introduction
contents.html_ja: 1 はじめに

contents.html: A hash algorithm is used to map a message of arbitrary length to a fixed-length message digest. Federal Information Processing Standard (FIPS) 180-4, the Secure Hash Standard (SHS) [FIPS 180-4], specifies seven approved hash algorithms: SHA-1, SHA-224, SHA-256, SHA-384, SHA-512, SHA-512/224 and SHA-512/256.
contents.html_ja: ハッシュアルゴリズムは、任意の長さのメッセージを固定長のメッセージダイジェストに対応付けるために使用される。連邦情報処理標準（FIPS）180-4「セキュアハッシュ標準（SHS）」[FIPS 180-4]は、承認済みハッシュアルゴリズムとして、SHA-1、SHA-224、SHA-256、SHA-384、SHA-512、SHA-512/224、SHA-512/256の7種類を規定している。

contents.html: This Recommendation provides security guidelines for supporting the required or desired security strengths of several cryptographic applications that employ the approved hash functions specified in FIPS 180-4, such as digital signature applications specified in FIPS 186-3 [FIPS 186-3], Keyed-hash Message Authentication Codes (HMACs) specified in FIPS 198-1 [FIPS 198-1] and Hash-based Key Derivation Functions specified in SP 800-56A [SP 800-56A] and SP 800-56B [SP 800-56B]. While the use of hash functions in HMAC-based key derivation functions is specified in SP 800-56C [SP 800-56C] and SP 800-108 [SP 800-108], these documents sufficiently address the security aspects of their use, so discussions of SP 800-56C and SP 800-108 are not included herein.
contents.html_ja: 本推奨事項は、FIPS 180-4で規定される承認済みハッシュ関数を使用する複数の暗号アプリケーションについて、要求される、または望ましいセキュリティ強度を確保するためのセキュリティ指針を示す。そのようなアプリケーションには、FIPS 186-3 [FIPS 186-3]で規定されるデジタル署名アプリケーション、FIPS 198-1 [FIPS 198-1]で規定される鍵付きハッシュメッセージ認証コード（HMAC）、SP 800-56A [SP 800-56A]およびSP 800-56B [SP 800-56B]で規定されるハッシュベース鍵導出関数などがある。HMACベースの鍵導出関数におけるハッシュ関数の使用はSP 800-56C [SP 800-56C]およびSP 800-108 [SP 800-108]で規定されているが、これらの文書がその使用のセキュリティ面を十分に扱っているため、本書ではSP 800-56CおよびSP 800-108について論じない。

contents.html: 3.1 Terms and Definitions
contents.html_ja: 3.1 用語と定義

contents.html: Adversary
contents.html_ja: 攻撃者

contents.html: An entity that is not authorized to access or modify information, or who works to defeat any protections afforded the information.
contents.html_ja: 情報へのアクセスまたは情報の変更を許可されていない主体、あるいは情報に施された保護を破ろうとする主体。

contents.html: Algorithm
contents.html_ja: アルゴリズム

contents.html: A clearly specified mathematical process for computation; a set of rules that, if followed, will give a prescribed result.
contents.html_ja: 計算のために明確に定められた数学的手順、すなわち、従えば所定の結果が得られる一連の規則。

contents.html: Approved
contents.html_ja: 承認済み

contents.html: FIPS-approved and/or NIST-recommended. An algorithm or technique that is either 1) specified in a FIPS or NIST Recommendation, 2) adopted in a FIPS or NIST Recommendation or 3) specified in a list of NIST-approved security functions.
contents.html_ja: FIPSで承認されたもの、および／またはNISTが推奨するもの。アルゴリズムまたは技法が、1) FIPSまたはNIST推奨事項で規定されている、2) FIPSまたはNIST推奨事項に採用されている、または3) NIST承認済みセキュリティ機能の一覧に記載されていることをいう。

contents.html: Approved hash algorithms
contents.html_ja: 承認済みハッシュアルゴリズム

contents.html: Hash algorithms specified in FIPS 180-4.
contents.html_ja: FIPS 180-4で規定されるハッシュアルゴリズム。

contents.html: Bit string
contents.html_ja: ビット列

contents.html: An ordered sequence of 0 and 1 bits. In this Recommendation, the leftmost bit is the most significant bit of the string. The rightmost bit is the least significant bit of the string.
contents.html_ja: 0と1を順序付けて並べた列。本推奨事項では、左端のビットを列の最上位ビット、右端のビットを最下位ビットとする。

contents.html: Bits of security
contents.html_ja: セキュリティビット数

contents.html: See security strength.
contents.html_ja: 「セキュリティ強度」を参照。

contents.html: Block cipher
contents.html_ja: ブロック暗号

contents.html: An invertible symmetric-key cryptographic algorithm that operates on fixed-length blocks of input using a secret key and an unvarying transformation algorithm. The resulting output block is the same length as the input block.
contents.html_ja: 秘密鍵と変化しない変換アルゴリズムを用い、固定長の入力ブロックを処理する、可逆な共通鍵暗号アルゴリズム。出力ブロックは入力ブロックと同じ長さである。

contents.html: Collision
contents.html_ja: 衝突

contents.html: An event in which two different messages have the same message digest.
contents.html_ja: 異なる2つのメッセージから同じメッセージダイジェストが得られる事象。

contents.html: Collision resistance
contents.html_ja: 衝突耐性

contents.html: An expected property of a hash function whereby it is computationally infeasible to find a collision, See “Collision”.
contents.html_ja: ハッシュ関数に期待される性質であり、衝突を見つけることが計算上実行不可能であることをいう。「衝突」を参照。

contents.html: Digital signature
contents.html_ja: デジタル署名

contents.html: The result of applying two cryptographic functions (a hash function, followed by a digital signature function; see FIPS 186-3 for details). When the functions are properly implemented, the digital signature provides origin authentication, data integrity protection and signatory non-repudiation.
contents.html_ja: 2つの暗号関数（ハッシュ関数に続いてデジタル署名関数）を適用した結果である。詳細はFIPS 186-3を参照。これらの関数が適切に実装されている場合、デジタル署名は発信元認証、データ完全性保護、および署名者の否認防止を実現する。

contents.html: Hash algorithm
contents.html_ja: ハッシュアルゴリズム

contents.html: See hash function. “Hash algorithm” and “hash function” are used interchangeably in this Recommendation.
contents.html_ja: 「ハッシュ関数」を参照。本推奨事項では「ハッシュアルゴリズム」と「ハッシュ関数」を同じ意味で使用する。

contents.html: Hash function
contents.html_ja: ハッシュ関数

contents.html: A function that maps a bit string of arbitrary length to a fixed-length bit string. The function is expected to have the following three properties:
contents.html_ja: 任意の長さのビット列を固定長のビット列に対応付ける関数。次の3つの性質を備えることが期待される。

contents.html: Collision resistance (see Collision resistance),
contents.html_ja: 衝突耐性（「衝突耐性」を参照）

contents.html: Preimage resistance (see Preimage resistance) and
contents.html_ja: 原像耐性（「原像耐性」を参照）、および

contents.html: Second preimage resistance (see Second preimage resistance).
contents.html_ja: 第二原像耐性（「第二原像耐性」を参照）。

contents.html: Approved hash functions are specified in [FIPS 180-4].
contents.html_ja: 承認済みハッシュ関数は[FIPS 180-4]で規定される。

contents.html: Hash output
contents.html_ja: ハッシュ出力

contents.html: See “message digest”.
contents.html_ja: 「メッセージダイジェスト」を参照。

contents.html: Hash value
contents.html_ja: ハッシュ値

contents.html: See “message digest”.
contents.html_ja: 「メッセージダイジェスト」を参照。

contents.html: Key
contents.html_ja: 鍵

contents.html: A parameter used with a cryptographic algorithm that determines its operation in such a way that an entity with knowledge of the key can reproduce or reverse the operation, while an entity without knowledge of the key cannot. Examples applicable to this Recommendation include:
contents.html_ja: 暗号アルゴリズムとともに使用され、その動作を決定するパラメータ。鍵を知る主体は処理を再現または逆転できるが、鍵を知らない主体にはそれができない。本推奨事項に関係する例を次に示す。

contents.html: The computation of a keyed-hash message authentication code.
contents.html_ja: 鍵付きハッシュメッセージ認証コードの計算。

contents.html: The verification of a keyed-hash message authentication code.
contents.html_ja: 鍵付きハッシュメッセージ認証コードの検証。

contents.html: The generation of a digital signature on a message.
contents.html_ja: メッセージに対するデジタル署名の生成。

contents.html: The verification of a digital signature.
contents.html_ja: デジタル署名の検証。

contents.html: Key Derivation Key
contents.html_ja: 鍵導出鍵

contents.html: A key used as an input to a key derivation function to derive other keys.
contents.html_ja: 別の鍵を導出するために、鍵導出関数への入力として使用する鍵。

contents.html: Keying Material
contents.html_ja: 鍵素材

contents.html: A bit string, such that any non-overlapping segments of the string with the required lengths can be used as symmetric cryptographic keys and secret parameters, such as initialization vectors.
contents.html_ja: 必要な長さを持つ、互いに重複しない任意の部分列を、共通鍵暗号鍵として、および初期化ベクトルなどの秘密パラメータとして使用できるビット列。

contents.html: L-bit Hash Function: A hash function for which the length of the output is L bits.
contents.html_ja: Lビットハッシュ関数：出力長がLビットのハッシュ関数。

contents.html: MAC algorithm: An algorithm that computes a MAC from a message and a key.
contents.html_ja: MACアルゴリズム：メッセージと鍵からMACを計算するアルゴリズム。

contents.html: Message digest
contents.html_ja: メッセージダイジェスト

contents.html: The result of applying a hash function to a message. Also known as a “hash value” or “hash output”.
contents.html_ja: メッセージにハッシュ関数を適用した結果。ハッシュ値またはハッシュ出力とも呼ばれる。

contents.html: Preimage
contents.html_ja: 原像

contents.html: A message X that produces a given message digest when it is processed by a hash function.
contents.html_ja: ハッシュ関数で処理したとき、所与のメッセージダイジェストを生成するメッセージX。

contents.html: Preimage resistance
contents.html_ja: 原像耐性

contents.html: An expected property of a hash function such that, given a randomly chosen message digest, message_digest, it is computationally infeasible to find a preimage of the message_digest, See “Preimage”.
contents.html_ja: ハッシュ関数に期待される性質であり、ランダムに選ばれたメッセージダイジェストmessage_digestが与えられたとき、それに対応する原像を見つけることが計算上実行不可能であることをいう。「原像」を参照。

contents.html: Random bit
contents.html_ja: ランダムビット

contents.html: A bit for which an attacker has exactly a 50% probability of success of guessing the value of the bit as either a zero or one. It is also called an unbiased bit.
contents.html_ja: 攻撃者がその値を0または1のいずれかと推測して成功する確率が正確に50%であるビット。偏りのないビットとも呼ばれる。

contents.html: Random bit generator
contents.html_ja: ランダムビット生成器

contents.html: A device or algorithm that can produce a sequence of bits that appear to be both statistically independent and unbiased.
contents.html_ja: 統計的に独立で偏りのないように見えるビット列を生成できる装置またはアルゴリズム。

contents.html: Randomized hashing: A process by which the input to a hash function is randomized before being processed by the hash function.
contents.html_ja: ランダム化ハッシュ：ハッシュ関数で処理する前に、その入力をランダム化する処理。

contents.html: Random number: A value in a set of numbers that has an equal probability of being selected from the total population of possibilities and, in that sense, is unpredictable. contents.html: 4.1 Hash Function Properties
contents.html_ja: 4.1 ハッシュ関数の特性

contents.html: An approved hash function1 is expected to have the following three properties:
contents.html_ja: 承認済みハッシュ関数1は、次の3つの性質を備えることが期待される。

contents.html: 1. Collision resistance: It is computationally infeasible to find two different inputs to the hash function that have the same hash value. That is, if \(\mathit{hash}\) is a hash function, it is computationally infeasible to find two different inputs \(x\) and \(x'\) for which \(\mathit{hash}(x) = \mathit{hash}(x')\). Collision resistance is measured by the amount of work that would be needed to find a collision for a hash function with high probability. If the amount of work is \(2^N\), then the collision resistance is \(N\) bits. The expected collision-resistance strength of a hash function is half the length of the hash value produced by that hash function, i.e., for an \(L\)-bit hash function, the expected security strength for collision resistance is \(L/2\) bits. For example, SHA-256 produces a (full-length) hash value of 256 bits; SHA-256 provides an expected collision resistance of 128 bits (see Table 1 in Section 4.2).
contents.html_ja: 1. 衝突耐性：同じハッシュ値となる、ハッシュ関数への異なる2つの入力を見つけることが計算上実行不可能であること。つまり、\(\mathit{hash}\)がハッシュ関数ならば、異なる2つの入力\(x\)と\(x'\)であって\(\mathit{hash}(x) = \mathit{hash}(x')\)となるものを見つけることが計算上実行不可能である。衝突耐性は、ハッシュ関数の衝突を高い確率で見つけるのに必要な作業量で測られる。必要な作業量が\(2^N\)なら、衝突耐性は\(N\)ビットである。ハッシュ関数の期待衝突耐性強度は、そのハッシュ関数が生成するハッシュ値の長さの半分である。すなわち、\(L\)ビットハッシュ関数の場合、衝突耐性の期待セキュリティ強度は\(L/2\)ビットとなる。例えば、SHA-256は256ビットの（全長）ハッシュ値を生成し、128ビットの期待衝突耐性を提供する（4.2節の表1を参照）。

contents.html: 1 The terms “hash function” and “hash algorithm” are used interchangeably, depending on the context of the discussions throughout this Recommendation.
contents.html_ja: 1 本推奨事項では、議論の文脈に応じて「ハッシュ関数」と「ハッシュアルゴリズム」を同じ意味で使用する。

contents.html: 2. Preimage resistance2: Given a randomly chosen hash value, \(\mathit{hash\_value}\), it is computationally infeasible to find an \(x\) so that \(\mathit{hash}(x) = \mathit{hash\_value}\). This property is also called the one-way property. Preimage resistance is measured by the amount of work that would be needed to have a high probability of finding a preimage for a hash function. If the amount of work is \(2^N\), then the preimage resistance is \(N\) bits. The expected preimage-resistance strength of a hash function is the length of the hash value produced by that hash function, i.e., for an \(L\)-bit hash function, the expected security strength for preimage resistance is \(L\) bits. For example, SHA-256 produces a (full-length) hash value of 256 bits; SHA-256 provides an expected preimage resistance of 256 bits (see Table 1 in Section 4.2).
contents.html_ja: 2. 原像耐性2：ランダムに選ばれたハッシュ値\(\mathit{hash\_value}\)が与えられたとき、\(x\)であって\(\mathit{hash}(x) = \mathit{hash\_value}\)となるものを見つけることが計算上実行不可能であること。この性質は一方向性とも呼ばれる。原像耐性は、ハッシュ関数の原像を高い確率で見つけるのに必要な作業量で測られる。必要な作業量が\(2^N\)なら、原像耐性は\(N\)ビットである。ハッシュ関数の期待原像耐性強度は、そのハッシュ関数が生成するハッシュ値の長さに等しい。すなわち、\(L\)ビットハッシュ関数の場合、原像耐性の期待セキュリティ強度は\(L\)ビットとなる。例えば、SHA-256は256ビットの（全長）ハッシュ値を生成し、256ビットの期待原像耐性を提供する（4.2節の表1を参照）。

contents.html: 3. Second preimage resistance: It is computationally infeasible to find a second input that has the same hash value as any other specified input. That is, given an input \(x\), it is computationally infeasible to find a second input \(x'\) that is different from \(x\), such that \(\mathit{hash}(x) = \mathit{hash}(x')\). Second preimage resistance is measured by the amount of work that would be needed to have a high probability of finding a second preimage for a hash function. If the amount of work is \(2^N\), then the second preimage resistance is \(N\) bits. In general, the expected second preimage strength of a hash function is the length of the hash value produced by that hash function, i.e., for an \(L\)-bit hash function, the expected security strength for second preimage resistance is \(L\) bits. For example, SHA-256 produces a (full-length) hash value of 256 bits; SHA-256 provides an expected second preimage resistance of 256 bits (see Table 1 in Section 4.2). However, for some hash functions, the second preimage resistance strength also depends on the message length processed by the hash function. More details can be found in Appendix A.
contents.html_ja: 3. 第二原像耐性：指定された任意の入力と同じハッシュ値を持つ第二の入力を見つけることが計算上実行不可能であること。つまり、入力\(x\)が与えられたとき、第二の入力\(x'\)であって、\(x\)とは異なり、\(\mathit{hash}(x) = \mathit{hash}(x')\)となるものを見つけることが計算上実行不可能である。第二原像耐性は、ハッシュ関数の第二原像を高い確率で見つけるのに必要な作業量で測られる。必要な作業量が\(2^N\)なら、第二原像耐性は\(N\)ビットである。一般に、ハッシュ関数の期待第二原像耐性強度は、そのハッシュ関数が生成するハッシュ値の長さに等しい。すなわち、\(L\)ビットハッシュ関数の場合、第二原像耐性の期待セキュリティ強度は\(L\)ビットとなる。例えば、SHA-256は256ビットの（全長）ハッシュ値を生成し、256ビットの期待第二原像耐性を提供する（4.2節の表1を参照）。ただし、一部のハッシュ関数では、第二原像耐性強度はハッシュ関数が処理するメッセージの長さにも依存する。詳細は付録Aを参照。

contents.html: The security strength of a hash function is determined by its collision resistance strength, preimage resistance strength or second preimage resistance strength, depending on the property(ies) that the cryptographic application needs from the hash function. If an application requires more than one property from the hash function, then the weakest property is the security strength of the hash function for that application. For instance, the security strength of a hash function for digital signatures is defined as its collision resistance strength, because digital signatures require both collision resistance and second preimage resistance from the hash function, and the collision resistance strength of the hash function (L/2) is less than its second preimage resistance strength (i.e., L). A hash function that is not suitable for one application might be suitable for other cryptographic applications that do not require the same security properties. SHA-1 is not suitable for general-purpose digital signature applications (as specified in FIPS 186-3) that require 112 bits of security. In the case of digital signatures, SHA-1 does not provide the 112 bits of collision resistance (see Table 1 in Section 4.2) needed to achieve the security strength. On the other hand, SHA-1 does provide the 112 bits of preimage resistance that is needed to achieve the 112-bit security strength for HMAC. The security strengths of the approved hash functions for different applications can be found in SP 800-57, Part 1 [SP 800-57].
contents.html_ja: ハッシュ関数のセキュリティ強度は、暗号アプリケーションがハッシュ関数に求める性質に応じて、衝突耐性強度、原像耐性強度、または第二原像耐性強度で決まる。アプリケーションが複数の性質を必要とする場合、そのハッシュ関数のセキュリティ強度は最も弱い性質によって決まる。例えば、デジタル署名では、ハッシュ関数に衝突耐性と第二原像耐性の両方が必要だが、衝突耐性強度（L/2）は第二原像耐性強度（L）より低いため、デジタル署名に用いるハッシュ関数のセキュリティ強度は衝突耐性強度として定義される。ある用途に適さないハッシュ関数でも、同じセキュリティ特性を必要としない別の暗号用途には適する場合がある。SHA-1は、112ビットのセキュリティを必要とする汎用デジタル署名アプリケーション（FIPS 186-3で規定）には適さない。デジタル署名では、必要なセキュリティ強度を満たすために必要な112ビットの衝突耐性をSHA-1は提供しない（4.2節の表1を参照）。一方、SHA-1はHMACで112ビットのセキュリティ強度を実現するために必要な112ビットの原像耐性を提供する。用途別の承認済みハッシュ関数のセキュリティ強度は、SP 800-57第1部[SP 800-57]を参照。

contents.html: As mentioned in Section 4.1, the expected collision resistance strength of any approved hash function is, in general, half the length of its hash value. This is currently believed to be true for all the approved hash functions except SHA-1. The latest cryptanalytic results for SHA-1 [SHA1 Attack] indicate that it may have a collision resistance strength that is considerably less than its expected strength of 80 bits. The expected preimage resistance strengths of the approved hash functions are provided in the above table. At the time that this Recommendation was written, there had been no known short cuts for finding preimages of the hash values generated by the approved hash algorithms. Except for SHA-384, SHA-512/224 and SHA-512/256, the second preimage resistance strengths of the approved hash functions depend not only on the functions themselves, but also on the sizes of the messages that the hash functions process [Second Preimage Attack]. In Table 1, the low end of each range applies to the situation where the length of the message input to the hash function is the maximum length allowed by the hash function, while the high end of the range applies to the situation where the message input length is relatively small. Information on determining the actual second preimage resistance strengths of the approved hash functions for different message lengths is provided in Appendix A. In the case of SHA-384, SHA-512/224 or SHA-512/256, the second preimage resistance strength does not depend on the message length; details can be found in Appendix A. Note that the preimage resistance and the second preimage resistance strengths are greater than the collision resistance strength for each of the approved hash algorithms specified in FIPS 180-4.

contents.html: 5.1 Truncated Message Digest
contents.html_ja: 5.1 切り詰められたメッセージダイジェスト

contents.html: Some applications may require a value that is shorter than the (full-length) message digest provided by an approved hash function as specified in FIPS 180-4. In such cases, it may be appropriate to use a subset of the bits produced by the hash function as the (shortened) message digest. Let the (shortened) message digest be called a truncated message digest, and let λ be its desired length in bits. A truncated message digest may be used if the following requirements are met:
contents.html_ja: 一部のアプリケーションでは、FIPS 180-4に規定される承認済みハッシュ関数が出力する（全長の）メッセージダイジェストより短い値が必要となる場合がある。そのような場合、ハッシュ関数が生成するビットの一部を（短縮された）メッセージダイジェストとして使用するのが適切なことがある。この（短縮された）メッセージダイジェストを「切り詰められたメッセージダイジェスト」と呼び、その所望のビット長をλとする。切り詰められたメッセージダイジェストは、次の要件を満たす場合に使用してよい。

contents.html: The length of the output block of the approved hash function to be used shall be greater than λ (i.e., L > λ).
contents.html_ja: 使用する承認済みハッシュ関数の出力ブロックの長さはλより大きくなければならない（すなわち、L > λ）。

contents.html: The λ left-most bits of the full-length message digest shall be selected as the truncated message digest.
contents.html_ja: 2. 全長メッセージダイジェストの左端からλビットを、切り詰められたメッセージダイジェストとして選択しなければならない。

contents.html: For example, if a truncated message digest of 96 bits is desired, the SHA-256 hash function could be used (e.g., because it is available to the application, and provides an output larger than 96 bits). The leftmost 96 bits of the 256-bit message digest generated by SHA-256 are selected as the truncated message digest, and the rightmost 160 bits of the message digest are discarded.
contents.html_ja: 例えば、96ビットの切り詰められたメッセージダイジェストが必要な場合、SHA-256ハッシュ関数を使用できる（例えば、アプリケーションで利用可能であり、96ビットを超える出力を提供するため）。SHA-256が生成する256ビットのメッセージダイジェストの左端96ビットを切り詰められたメッセージダイジェストとして選択し、右端の160ビットを破棄する。

contents.html: 3. If collision resistance is required, \(\lambda\) shall be at least twice the required collision resistance strength \(s\) (in bits) for the truncated message digest (i.e., \(\lambda \ge 2s\)).
contents.html_ja: 3. 衝突耐性が必要な場合、\(\lambda\)は、切り詰められたメッセージダイジェストに必要な衝突耐性強度\(s\)（ビット単位）の少なくとも2倍でなければならない（すなわち、\(\lambda \ge 2s\)）。

contents.html: These specifications for truncating the output of a cryptographic hash function promote application interoperability in situations where the use of shortened message digests is appropriate (and permissible), as determined by implementers and application developers acting in conformance with NIST Standards and Recommendations. Truncating the message digest can impact the security of an application. By truncating a message digest, the expected collision resistance strength is reduced from L/2 to λ/2 (in bits). For the example in item 2 above, even though SHA-256 provides 128 bits of collision resistance, the collision resistance provided by the 96-bit truncated message digest is half the length of the truncated message digest, which is 48 bits, in this case.
contents.html_ja: 暗号ハッシュ関数の出力を切り詰めるこれらの仕様は、NIST標準および推奨事項に従う実装者とアプリケーション開発者が適切かつ許容できると判断した場合に、短縮されたメッセージダイジェストを使用する状況で、アプリケーション間の相互運用性を促進する。メッセージダイジェストの切り詰めは、アプリケーションのセキュリティに影響することがある。切り詰めると、期待衝突耐性強度はL/2からλ/2（ビット単位）へ低下する。上記の項目2の例では、SHA-256自体は128ビットの衝突耐性を提供するが、96ビットに切り詰めたメッセージダイジェストの衝突耐性は、その長さの半分、すなわち48ビットとなる。

contents.html: The truncated message digest of λ bits provides an expected preimage resistance of λ bits, not L bits, regardless of the hash function used. The expected second preimage resistance strength of a message digest truncated to λ bits sometimes depends on the length of the message. This dependence is determined as specified in Appendix A. Note that there are situations for which the expected second preimage resistance strength does not depend on the message length. For example, a 130-bit truncated message digest generated using SHA-256 has an expected second preimage strength of 130 bits, rather than a value in the range specified in Table 1 above for SHA-256. Truncating the message digest can have other impacts, as well. For example, applications that use a truncated message digest risk attacks based on confusion between different parties about the specific amount of truncation used, as well as the specific hash function that was used to produce the truncated message digest. Any application using a truncated message digest is responsible for ensuring that the truncation amount and the hash function used are known to all parties, with no chance of ambiguity.
contents.html_ja: λビットに切り詰めたメッセージダイジェストが提供する期待原像耐性は、使用するハッシュ関数にかかわらずLビットではなくλビットである。λビットに切り詰めたメッセージダイジェストの期待第二原像耐性強度は、メッセージ長に依存することがある。この依存関係は付録Aの規定に従って決まる。期待第二原像耐性強度がメッセージ長に依存しない場合もある。例えば、SHA-256で生成した130ビットの切り詰められたメッセージダイジェストの期待第二原像耐性強度は130ビットであり、表1に示したSHA-256の範囲内の値ではない。メッセージダイジェストの切り詰めには、ほかの影響もある。例えば、切り詰められたメッセージダイジェストを使うアプリケーションでは、切り詰め量や生成に用いたハッシュ関数について当事者間に混乱が生じることで、攻撃の危険が生じる。切り詰められたメッセージダイジェストを使用するアプリケーションは、曖昧さが生じないよう、切り詰め量と使用したハッシュ関数をすべての当事者が把握できるようにする責任を負う。

contents.html: 5.2 Digital Signatures
contents.html_ja: 5.2 デジタル署名

contents.html: A hash function is used to map a message of any eligible length (see FIPS 180-4) to a fixed-length message digest. In a digital signature generation process, this message digest is then signed by a signing operation, such as an RSA private key operation, to produce a digital signature. The resulting digital signature is used to verify who signed the message and whether or not the message was altered (either deliberately or accidentally) after it was signed. When two different messages have the same message digest (i.e., a collision is found), then a digital signature of one message could be used as a digital signature for the other message. If this happens, then a verified digital signature does not guarantee the authenticity of the signed message, because either one of the two messages could be considered valid. Therefore, a hash function used for digital signatures requires collision resistance. The approved hash functions are considered to provide the collision resistance strengths as specified in Table 1 of Section 4.2. For digital signature applications, the security strength of a hash function without any preprocessing is generally its collision resistance strength. When appropriate processing is applied to the data before the hash value is computed, the security strength may be more than the collision resistance strength (see Section 5.2.3). Without any preprocessing of the message input to the hash function, the security strength of any digital signature that is generated using an algorithm specified in FIPS 186-3 is the minimum of the collision resistance strength of the hash algorithm and the security strength provided by the signing algorithm. More information on security strengths can be found in SP 800-57, Part 1. For instance, if a digital signature that is generated by one of the approved digital signature algorithms with SHA-1 as the hash function and key sizes specified in FIPS 186-33, then the security strength of this digital signature is less than 80 bits (see Table 1 in Section 4.2); i.e., the strength of the digital signature process is determined by the strength of SHA-1, rather than the strength of the key, in this case. Therefore, SHA-1 shall not be used in any new digital signature applications that require at least 80 bits of security strength. Furthermore, SHA-1 shall not be used for the generation of digital signatures after the end of 2013 (see SP 800-131A [SP 800-131A] for information about the required key lengths for digital signature applications). More information on the security strengths of digital signature applications using the approved hash algorithms and the recommended lifetimes of cryptographic algorithm usage can be found in SP 800-57, Part 1. There are several ways to use hash functions with digital signature algorithms as described below.
contents.html_ja: ハッシュ関数は、FIPS 180-4で認められる長さのメッセージを固定長のメッセージダイジェストに対応付けるために使用される。デジタル署名の生成では、このメッセージダイジェストに署名操作（RSA秘密鍵操作など）を適用し、デジタル署名を生成する。生成されたデジタル署名は、誰がメッセージに署名したか、また署名後にメッセージが（意図的または偶発的に）変更されたかどうかを検証するために使われる。異なる2つのメッセージが同じメッセージダイジェストを持つ（すなわち衝突が見つかる）場合、一方のメッセージのデジタル署名を他方のメッセージの署名として使用できてしまう。この場合、どちらのメッセージも有効とみなされ得るため、署名を検証できても、署名されたメッセージの真正性は保証されない。したがって、デジタル署名に用いるハッシュ関数には衝突耐性が必要である。承認済みハッシュ関数は、4.2節の表1に示す衝突耐性強度を提供するとみなされている。デジタル署名アプリケーションでは、前処理を一切行わない場合のハッシュ関数のセキュリティ強度は、一般にその衝突耐性強度である。ハッシュ値の計算前にデータへ適切な処理を適用する場合、セキュリティ強度は衝突耐性強度を上回ることがある（5.2.3節を参照）。ハッシュ関数へのメッセージ入力を前処理しない場合、FIPS 186-3で規定されるアルゴリズムで生成されるデジタル署名のセキュリティ強度は、ハッシュアルゴリズムの衝突耐性強度と署名アルゴリズムのセキュリティ強度の小さい方となる。セキュリティ強度の詳細はSP 800-57第1部を参照。例えば、承認済みデジタル署名アルゴリズムのいずれかを使い、ハッシュ関数としてSHA-1を用い、FIPS 186-3で規定された鍵長³で生成したデジタル署名のセキュリティ強度は80ビット未満である（4.2節の表1を参照）。この場合、署名プロセスの強度は鍵の強度ではなくSHA-1の強度で決まる。したがって、少なくとも80ビットのセキュリティ強度を必要とする新たなデジタル署名アプリケーションでSHA-1を使用してはならない。さらに、2013年末以降、デジタル署名の生成にSHA-1を使用してはならない（デジタル署名アプリケーションで必要な鍵長についてはSP 800-131A [SP 800-131A]を参照）。承認済みハッシュアルゴリズムを用いるデジタル署名アプリケーションのセキュリティ強度と、暗号アルゴリズムの推奨使用期間については、SP 800-57第1部を参照。以下に、デジタル署名アルゴリズムでハッシュ関数を使用する複数の方法を示す。

contents.html: 5.2.1 Full-length Message Digests
contents.html_ja: 5.2.1 全長メッセージダイジェスト

contents.html: When the untruncated output of an approved hash function (as specified in FIPS 180-4) is used by an approved digital signature algorithm (as specified in FIPS 186-3), the resulting full-length message digests can support security strengths up to those given in Table 1 of Section 4.2 (for collision resistance).

contents.html: 5.2.2 Truncated Message Digests
contents.html_ja: 5.2.2 切り詰められたメッセージダイジェスト

contents.html: In some specific situations, truncated message digests are used in generating digital signatures. (Details about these situations, including the lengths required for the truncated hash values, can be found in FIPS 186-3.) In such cases, the security strength that can be supported by a hash function depends on the length of these truncated values, as well as the particular hash function that is used. As noted in Section 5.1, when the outputs of an approved \(L\)-bit hash function are truncated to \(\lambda\) bits (where \(\lambda < L\)), the collision resistance strength supported by the truncated message digests is reduced to \(\lambda/2\) bits. Therefore, in addition to the requirements/restrictions imposed by FIPS 186-3, the value of \(\lambda\) shall be at least twice the desired security strength (in bits) required for the digital signature. For example, if a security strength of 112 bits is required for digital signatures, a (truncated) message digest of (at least) 224 bits must be used. If required/desired, any approved hash functions except SHA-1 could be employed to generate (truncated) message digests of exactly 224 bits in length. (For SHA-224 and SHA-512/224, the hash function's output would not require truncation.) It is recommended that the hash function chosen should minimize the number of truncation operations required to achieve the required/desired length for the hash value. For the 224-bit example above, SHA-512/224 should be chosen over SHA-384 and SHA-512/256. All three hash functions employ one (internal) truncation operation to produce their output, but SHA-384 and SHA-512/256 would each require an additional (external) truncation operation to pare their output down to the desired length of 224 bits.
contents.html_ja: 特定の状況では、デジタル署名の生成に切り詰められたメッセージダイジェストを使用する（必要な切り詰めハッシュ値の長さを含む状況の詳細はFIPS 186-3を参照）。この場合、ハッシュ関数が支えられるセキュリティ強度は、切り詰められた値の長さと使用するハッシュ関数の両方に依存する。5.1節で述べたとおり、承認済み\(L\)ビットハッシュ関数の出力を\(\lambda\)ビットに切り詰める場合（\(\lambda < L\)）、切り詰められたメッセージダイジェストが支える衝突耐性強度は\(\lambda/2\)ビットに低下する。したがって、FIPS 186-3が課す要件および制限に加えて、\(\lambda\)の値はデジタル署名に必要な目標セキュリティ強度（ビット単位）の少なくとも2倍でなければならない。例えば、デジタル署名に112ビットのセキュリティ強度が必要なら、少なくとも224ビットの（切り詰められた）メッセージダイジェストを使用しなければならない。必要または望ましい場合、SHA-1を除く任意の承認済みハッシュ関数を使って、正確に224ビット長の（切り詰められた）メッセージダイジェストを生成できる（SHA-224およびSHA-512/224では、ハッシュ関数の出力を切り詰める必要はない）。必要または望ましいハッシュ値長を得るために必要な切り詰め操作の回数が最小となるハッシュ関数を選ぶことが推奨される。上記の224ビットの例では、SHA-384やSHA-512/256よりSHA-512/224を選ぶべきである。3つのハッシュ関数はいずれも出力を生成するために内部切り詰めを1回行うが、SHA-384とSHA-512/256では、出力を目標の224ビットにするため、さらに外部切り詰めを行う必要がある。

contents.html: 5.2.3 Randomized Hashing for Digital Signatures
contents.html_ja: 5.2.3 デジタル署名のためのランダム化ハッシュ

contents.html: As described in Section 5.2, the overall security strength of a digital signature is limited by the collision resistance strength of the hash function. However, when using the randomized hashing technique specified in SP 800-106 [SP 800-106], a randomized hash function may support a higher level of security with respect to a particular potential vulnerability, offering enhanced protection to a message signer against a collision attack by a malicious message preparer who formulates the message to be signed, but does not actually sign the message. In such an attack, the malicious message preparer would endeavor to find two messages that hash to the same value. Once the message signer had generated a signature for one of the messages, the malicious preparer could accuse the signer of having signed the other message instead. In situations where one party is asked to sign messages prepared by another party, the level of protection (in bits) that is provided to the message signer against a collision attack by using randomized hashing is determined by the minimum of the following three quantities:
contents.html_ja: 5.2節で説明したように、デジタル署名全体のセキュリティ強度はハッシュ関数の衝突耐性強度によって制限される。ただし、SP 800-106 [SP 800-106]で規定されるランダム化ハッシュ技法を用いると、特定の潜在的な脆弱性に対するセキュリティ強度を高められる場合がある。実際には署名せず、署名対象のメッセージを作成する悪意あるメッセージ作成者が衝突攻撃を行う場合に、ランダム化ハッシュ関数は署名者をより強く保護できる。この攻撃では、悪意ある作成者は同じ値にハッシュされる2つのメッセージを見つけようとする。署名者が一方のメッセージに署名した後、作成者は、署名者がもう一方のメッセージに署名したと主張できる。ある当事者が別の当事者の用意したメッセージへの署名を求められる状況で、ランダム化ハッシュによる衝突攻撃への署名者の保護レベル（ビット単位）は、次の3つの値の最小値で決まる。

contents.html: The second preimage resistance strength (in bits) of the hash function.
contents.html_ja: 1. ハッシュ関数の第二原像耐性強度（ビット単位）。

contents.html: The security strength (in bits) of the random bit generator (RBG) employed by the signer to produce bit strings used to randomize messages, or, the collision resistance strength (in bits) of the hash function – whichever is larger.
contents.html_ja: 2. 署名者がメッセージをランダム化するビット列の生成に用いるランダムビット生成器（RBG）のセキュリティ強度（ビット単位）、またはハッシュ関数の衝突耐性強度（ビット単位）のうち、大きい方。

contents.html: The sum of the collision resistance strength (in bits) of the hash function and the smaller of these two quantities: (1) The length (in bits) of bit strings used to randomize messages (denoted rv in SP 800-106), and (2) The length (in bits) of the RBG output used to generate rv (as specified in Section 3.3 of SP 800-106).
contents.html_ja: 3. ハッシュ関数の衝突耐性強度（ビット単位）と、次の2つの値の小さい方との合計：(1) メッセージのランダム化に使うビット列の長さ（ビット単位、SP 800-106ではrvと表記）、(2) rvの生成に使うRBG出力の長さ（ビット単位、SP 800-106第3.3節で規定）。

contents.html: When randomized hashing is used, the RBG (see Section 5.5 below for more information) employed to produce the bit strings used to randomize messages shall support a security strength that is equal to or greater than the security strength of the signing algorithm. See SP 800-57, Part 1, for information about security strengths of different signing algorithms. The randomization process itself shall conform to the specifications of SP 800-106 for digital signature applications supporting at least 112 bits of security. Under these conditions, SHA-1-based randomized hashing could provide 112 bits of security strength against a collision attack by a malicious message preparer, even though the unrandomized SHA-1 function has a collision resistance strength that is less than 80 bits. It is important to note what the use of randomized hashing for digital signatures does and does not provide:
contents.html_ja: ランダム化ハッシュを使用する場合、メッセージのランダム化に用いるビット列を生成するRBG（詳細は後述の5.5節を参照）は、署名アルゴリズムのセキュリティ強度以上のセキュリティ強度を支えなければならない。各種署名アルゴリズムのセキュリティ強度についてはSP 800-57第1部を参照。ランダム化処理自体は、112ビット以上のセキュリティを支えるデジタル署名アプリケーションについて、SP 800-106の仕様に適合しなければならない。この条件下では、ランダム化していないSHA-1関数の衝突耐性強度が80ビット未満でも、SHA-1ベースのランダム化ハッシュは、悪意あるメッセージ作成者による衝突攻撃に対して112ビットのセキュリティ強度を提供できる。デジタル署名にランダム化ハッシュを使うことで得られるものと得られないものを理解しておくことが重要である。

contents.html: 1) Randomized hashing can offer a message signer additional protection by reducing the likelihood that a message preparer can find multiple messages that yield the same hash value during the digital signature generation process – even if it is practical to find collisions for the unrandomized hash function.
contents.html_ja: 1) ランダム化ハッシュは、ランダム化していないハッシュ関数で衝突を実際に見つけられる場合でも、デジタル署名生成中にメッセージ作成者が同じハッシュ値になる複数のメッセージを見つける可能性を下げ、署名者を追加的に保護できる。

contents.html: 2) Randomized hashing does not offer the message preparer or the signature verifiers any additional protection from a misbehaving signer (who may, for example, generate one signature that can be associated with either of two chosen messages after finding randomized versions of those messages that hash to the same value).
contents.html_ja: 2) ランダム化ハッシュは、不正な署名者（例えば、選択した2つのメッセージについて同じ値にハッシュされるランダム化版を見つけた後、その2つのメッセージのどちらにも対応付けられる1つの署名を生成し得る署名者）から、メッセージ作成者や署名検証者を追加的に保護するものではない。

contents.html: Randomized hashing does not improve the assurance of origin authenticity, data integrity, and/or signatory non-repudiation provided by the digital signature to signature verifiers (i.e., relying parties).
contents.html_ja: ランダム化ハッシュは、デジタル署名が署名検証者（すなわち依拠当事者）に提供する発信元真正性、データ完全性、および／または署名者の否認防止に関する保証を高めるものではない。

contents.html: 5.3 Keyed-Hash Message Authentication Codes (HMAC)
contents.html_ja: 5.3 鍵付きハッシュメッセージ認証コード（HMAC）

contents.html: 5.3.1 Description

Message authentication codes (MACs) provide data authentication and integrity protection. Two types of algorithms for computing a MAC have been approved: 1) MAC algorithms that are based on approved block cipher algorithms (more information can be found in [SPs 800-38B, C and D]) and 2) MAC algorithms that are based on hash functions, called HMAC algorithms, that are specified in FIPS 198-1. This section discusses the use of HMAC. An output from an HMAC algorithm is called an HMAC output. The HMAC output is either used in its entirety, or is truncated (see Section 5.3.3) when it is transmitted for subsequent verification. The transmitted value is called a MacTag. The HMAC algorithm requires the use of a secret key that is shared between the entity that generates the HMAC output (e.g., a message sender), and the entity (or entities) that need to verify the transmitted MacTag (message receiver(s)). The HMAC output is generated from a secret key and the string of “text” to be MACed (e.g., a message to be sent) using the HMAC algorithm. The MacTag is provided to the MacTag verifier, along with the “text” that was MACed (e.g., the sender transmits both the MacTag and the message to the intended receiver). The verifier computes an HMAC output on the received “text” using the same key and HMAC algorithm that were (purportedly) used to generate the received MacTag, generates a (new) MacTag (either a full or truncated HMAC output), and then compares the verifier-generated MacTag with the received MacTag. If the two values match, the “text” has been correctly received and the verifier is assured that the entity that generated the MacTag is a member of the community of users that share the key. The security strength provided by the HMAC algorithm depends on the security strength of the HMAC key, the underlying hash algorithm and the length of the MacTag.
contents.html_ja: メッセージ認証コード（MAC）は、データの認証と完全性保護を提供する。MACの計算には、承認済みブロック暗号アルゴリズムに基づくMACアルゴリズム（詳細は[SP 800-38B、C、D]を参照）と、ハッシュ関数に基づくMACアルゴリズムの2種類が承認されている。後者はHMACアルゴリズムと呼ばれ、FIPS 198-1で規定される。本節ではHMACの使用について説明する。HMACアルゴリズムの出力をHMAC出力と呼ぶ。後続の検証のために送信するとき、HMAC出力は全体を使用するか、切り詰める（5.3.3節を参照）。送信される値をMacTagと呼ぶ。HMACアルゴリズムでは、HMAC出力を生成する主体（例えばメッセージ送信者）と、送信されたMacTagを検証する必要がある主体（複数の場合もある、すなわちメッセージ受信者）との間で秘密鍵を共有する必要がある。HMACアルゴリズムを使い、秘密鍵とMAC対象の「テキスト」列（例えば送信するメッセージ）からHMAC出力を生成する。MacTagは、MAC対象の「テキスト」とともに検証者へ渡される（例えば、送信者はMacTagとメッセージを意図した受信者へ送信する）。検証者は、受信した「テキスト」に対し、受信したMacTagの生成に使われた（とされる）ものと同じ鍵とHMACアルゴリズムでHMAC出力を計算し、新しいMacTag（HMAC出力の全体または切り詰めた値）を生成して、検証者が生成したMacTagと受信したMacTagを比較する。2つの値が一致すれば、「テキスト」は正しく受信されており、検証者はMacTagを生成した主体が鍵を共有する利用者群の一員であると確信できる。HMACアルゴリズムが提供するセキュリティ強度は、HMAC鍵のセキュリティ強度、基礎となるハッシュアルゴリズム、およびMacTagの長さに依存する。

contents.html: 5.3.2 The HMAC Key
contents.html_ja: 5.3.2 HMAC鍵

contents.html: The security strength of the HMAC algorithm depends, in part, on the security strength of the HMAC key, K. An HMAC key shall have a security strength that meets or exceeds the security strength required to protect the data over which the HMAC is computed.
contents.html_ja: HMACアルゴリズムのセキュリティ強度は、HMAC鍵Kのセキュリティ強度にも依存する。HMAC鍵は、HMACを計算する対象データの保護に必要なセキュリティ強度以上でなければならない。

contents.html: The HMAC key shall be kept secret. When the secrecy of the HMAC key, K, is not preserved, an adversary that knows K, may impersonate any of the users that share that key in order to generate MacTags that seem to be authentic (i.e., MacTags that can be verified and are subsequently presumed to be authentic). contents.html: Let \(C\) denote the bit length of the internal hash value that is denoted \(H\) in FIPS 180-4. (This \(H\) is often called the “chaining value” in descriptions of Merkle–Damgård-style hash functions.) Note that \(C\) is not (necessarily) equal to \(L\), the bit length of the hash function’s output (see, for example, SHA-384 or SHA-512/\(t\) for any \(t < 512\), for which \(L < 512 = C\)). In all currently approved hash functions, \(L \le C\) (with \(L = C\) for SHA-1, SHA-256, and SHA-512). The effective security strength4 of the HMAC key is the minimum of the security strength of \(K\) and the value of \(2C\). That is, \(\text{security strength} = \min(\text{security strength of } K, 2C)\). For example, if the security strength of \(K\) is 128 bits, and SHA-1 is used, then the effective security strength of the HMAC key is 128 bits, since for SHA-1, \(2C = 320\). Note that, in this example, even if the security strength of \(K\) is greater than 320 bits, the effective security strength of the key is limited to 320 bits (the value of \(2C\) for SHA-1). In general, there is no benefit in generating \(K\) with more than \(2C\) bits of security. In particular, it is not sensible to generate \(K\) with a bit length that exceeds the input block size of the approved \(L\)-bit hash function employed in the HMAC construction. Such a \(K\) is hashed, and the resulting \(L\)-bit value is used instead. Returning to the SHA-1 example, suppose that the key \(K\) has a bit length greater than 512 (the input block size for SHA-1). Instead of using \(K\) directly, HMAC replaces \(K\) by its 160-bit SHA-1 hash value, and so the effective security strength of that choice of \(K\) is no more than 160 bits.

contents.html: The successful verification of a \(\mathit{MacTag}\) does not completely guarantee that the accompanying text is authentic; there is a slight chance that an adversary with no knowledge of the HMAC key, \(K\), can present a \((\mathit{MacTag}, \mathit{text})\) pair that will pass the verification procedure. From the perspective of an adversary that does not know the HMAC key \(K\) (i.e., the adversary is not among the community of users that share the key), the assurance of authenticity provided by a \(\mathit{MacTag}\) depends on its length and on the number of failed \(\mathit{MacTag}\) verifications allowed by a system for each value of the HMAC key. Let \(2^t\) be the number of failed \(\mathit{MacTag}\) verifications allowed by a system for each value of the HMAC key. The \(\mathit{MacTag}\) length, \(\lambda\), and the value of \(t\) need to be chosen to avoid an unacceptable probability of falsely accepting forged data. The likelihood of accepting forged data as authentic is \((1/2)^{(\lambda - t)}\). For example, if \(\lambda\) is 32, and a system allows \(2^{12}\) failed \(\mathit{MacTag}\) verifications for any given value of the HMAC key, then the likelihood of accepting forged data is \((1/2)^{20}\). In order to increase assurance of authenticity, either \(\lambda\) would need to be increased, or the number of allowed failed \(\mathit{MacTag}\) verifications for each value of the HMAC key would need to be decreased. To avoid having an unacceptable probability of falsely accepting forged data at any time, the value of the HMAC key must be changed to a new value before the number of failed \(\mathit{MacTag}\) authentications reaches the maximum allowed number (\(2^t\)). For the example above, with \(\lambda = 32\) and \(t = 20\), the HMAC key must be changed before the number of failed \(\mathit{MacTag}\) verifications reaches \(2^{12}\). The table below provides the likelihoods of accepting forged data for different \(\mathit{MacTag}\) lengths and allowed numbers of MAC verifications using a given value of the HMAC key. This table is intended to assist the implementers of HMAC applications in security-sensitive systems to assess the security risk associated with using \(\mathit{MacTags}\).

contents.html: Hash functions can be used as building blocks in key derivation functions (KDFs) (e.g., as specified in SP 800-56A, SP 800-56B, SP 800-56C and SP 800-108). The KDFs specified in future versions of SPs 800-56A and B are expected to use the hash functions either directly or indirectly in an HMAC construction. The method specified in SP 800-56C is an additional approved method for key derivation purposes in SPs 800-56A and B. The key derivation functions in SP 800-56A, B and C are used to generate (i.e., derive) secret keying material from a shared secret computed during a key agreement transaction between communicating parties. The hash-based KDFs specified in SP 800-108 use an HMAC construction and can be used either: (1) to derive keying material from an existing key, or (2) as a key-expansion step in the key derivation method specified in SP 800-56C. In addition to the KDFs in SPs 800-56A, B and C, and in SP 800-108, there are several other allowed application-specific KDFs described in SP 800-135 [SP 800-135]. These application-specific KDFs are approved for use in their own protocols with specific conditions; see SP 800-135 for detailed information.

contents.html: SP 800-56C specifies a two-step key derivation procedure, which is also known as an “extraction-then-expansion” procedure. This procedure is included by reference in SPs 800-56A and B. The extraction-then-expansion procedure in SP 800-56C is comprised of two separate steps: randomness-extraction and key-expansion, both of which can be implemented using an HMAC construction; when this construction is used, the same hash function is used for the randomness extraction and key expansion steps. The security strength that can be provided by a key derived using the two-step procedure depends on the security strength of the asymmetric keys used to generate the shared secret, the preimage strength of the hash function used in each HMAC construction and the length of the derived key. In the randomness extraction step, the key used for HMAC is a salt, which can be a publicly known value, a secret value, or a combination of both; the result of this step is a key derivation key. contents.html: In an application, if the size of the messages is small, then the second preimage resistance strengths of the hash functions are practically the same as their preimage resistance strengths described in Section 4.2. The actual second preimage resistance strength for SHA-1, SHA -224, SHA-256 and SHA-512 is approximately \((L - M)\), where \(L\) is the output block size of the hash function, and the message is \(2^M\) input blocks in length. For example, if a message that is \(2^{33}\) bits in length (i.e., a gigabyte long) is hashed by SHA-256 (whose input block size is \(2^9\) bits), the second preimage resistance strength is \((L - M) = (256 - 24) = 232\) bits (where \(L = 256\), and \(M = \log_2(2^{33}/2^9) = (33 - 9) = 24\)). That is, the amount of work required to find a second preimage is \(2^{232}\).

contents.html: It is important to note that the amount of work is based on the number of compression function executions (compressing single message blocks), not on the number of hash function executions (hashing messages of more than one block in length). The actual second preimage resistance strength of SHA-1, SHA -224, SHA-256 and SHA-512 varies, depending on the maximum size of the messages in the application using the hash function. The second preimage resistance of SHA-384, SHA-512/224 or SHA-512/256 does not depend on the message length because the attack described in [Second Preimage Attack] would actually require more work than a brute-force approach, which will break the second preimage resistance of SHA-384, SHA-512/224 or SHA-512/256 with work of 384, 224, or 256 bits, respectively. For any truncated message digest of λ bits, the actual second preimage resistance strength of SHA-1, SHA-224, SHA-256, and SHA-512 is the minimum of (L – M) and λ, where λ ≤ 160 for SHA-1, λ ≤ 224 for SHA-224, λ ≤ 256 for SHA-256, and λ ≤ 512 for SHA-512. The actual second preimage resistance strengths of SHA-384, SHA-512/224 and SHA-512/256 is λ (where λ ≤ 384 for SHA-384, λ ≤ 224 for SHA-512/224, and λ ≤ 256 for SHA-512/256).
contents.html_ja: 重要なのは、計算量がハッシュ関数の実行回数（複数ブロックから成るメッセージのハッシュ回数）ではなく、圧縮関数の実行回数（単一メッセージブロックを圧縮する回数）に基づく点である。SHA-1、SHA -224、SHA-256およびSHA-512の実際の第二原像耐性強度は、そのハッシュ関数を使うアプリケーションで扱うメッセージの最大サイズによって変わる。SHA-384、SHA-512/224またはSHA-512/256の第二原像耐性はメッセージ長に依存しない。[Second Preimage Attack]で説明されている攻撃は、実際には総当たり法よりも多くの計算量を要するためである。総当たり法は、SHA-384、SHA-512/224またはSHA-512/256の第二原像耐性を、それぞれ384、224、256ビットの計算量で破る。λビットに切り詰めた任意のメッセージダイジェストについて、SHA-1、SHA-224、SHA-256およびSHA-512の実際の第二原像耐性強度は（L−M）とλの小さい方である。ここで、SHA-1ではλ≤160、SHA-224ではλ≤224、SHA-256ではλ≤256、SHA-512ではλ≤512である。SHA-384、SHA-512/224およびSHA-512/256の実際の第二原像耐性強度はλである（ここで、SHA-384ではλ≤384、SHA-512/224ではλ≤224、SHA-512/256ではλ≤256）。

original_blocks.html: Collision resistance: It is computationally infeasible to find two different inputs to the hash function that have the same hash value. That is, if hash is a hash function, it is computationally infeasible to find two different inputs x and x’ for which hash(x) = hash(x’). Collision resistance is measured by the amount of work that would be needed to find a collision for a hash function with high probability. If the amount of work is 2<sup>N</sup>, then the collision resistance is N bits. The expected collision-resistance strength of a hash function is half the length of the hash value produced by that hash function, i.e., for an L-bit hash function, the expected security strength for collision resistance is L/2 bits. For example, SHA-256 produces a (full-length) hash value of 256 bits; SHA-256 provides an expected collision resistance of 128 bits (see Table 1 in Section 4.2).
original_blocks.html_ja: 衝突耐性：同じハッシュ値となる、ハッシュ関数への異なる2つの入力を見つけることが計算上実行不可能であること。つまり、hashがハッシュ関数ならば、hash(x) = hash(x’)となる異なる2つの入力xとx’を見つけることが計算上実行不可能である。衝突耐性は、ハッシュ関数の衝突を高い確率で見つけるのに必要な作業量で測られる。必要な作業量が2<sup>N</sup>なら、衝突耐性はNビットである。ハッシュ関数の期待衝突耐性強度は、そのハッシュ関数が生成するハッシュ値の長さの半分である。すなわち、Lビットハッシュ関数の場合、衝突耐性の期待セキュリティ強度はL/2ビットとなる。例えば、SHA-256は256ビットの（全長）ハッシュ値を生成し、128ビットの期待衝突耐性を提供する（4.2節の表1を参照）。

original_blocks.html: Preimage resistance2: Given a randomly chosen hash value, hash_value, it is computationally infeasible to find an x so that hash(x) = hash_value. This property is also called the one-way property. Preimage resistance is measured by the amount of work that would be needed to have a high probability of finding a preimage for a hash function. If the amount of work is 2<sup>N</sup>, then the preimage resistance is N bits. The expected preimage-resistance strength of a hash function is the length of the hash value produced by that hash function, i.e., for an L-bit hash function, the expected security strength for preimage resistance is L bits. For example, SHA-256 produces a (full-length) hash value of 256 bits; SHA-256 provides an expected preimage resistance of 256 bits (see Table 1 in Section 4.2).

original_blocks.html: Second preimage resistance: It is computationally infeasible to find a second input that has the same hash value as any other specified input. That is, given an input x, it is computationally infeasible to find a second input x’ that is different from x, such that hash(x) = hash(x’). Second preimage resistance is measured by the amount of work that would be needed to have a high probability of finding a second preimage for a hash function. If the amount of work is 2<sup>N</sup>, then the second preimage resistance is N bits. In general, the expected second preimage strength of a hash function is the length of the hash value produced by that hash function, i.e., for an L-bit hash function, the expected security strength for second preimage resistance is L bits. For example, SHA-256 produces a (full-length) hash value of 256 bits; SHA-256 provides an expected second preimage resistance of 256 bits (see Table 1 in Section 4.2). However, for some hash functions, the second preimage resistance strength also depends on the message length processed by the hash function. More details can be found in Appendix A.

original_blocks.html: In some specific situations, truncated message digests are used in generating digital signatures. (Details about these situations, including the lengths required for the truncated hash values, can be found in FIPS 186-3.) In such cases, the security strength that can be supported by a hash function depends on the length of these truncated values, as well as the particular hash function that is used. As noted in Section 5.1, when the outputs of an approved L-bit hash function are truncated to λ bits (where λ < L), the collision resistance strength supported by the truncated message digests is reduced to λ /2 bits. Therefore, in addition to the requirements/restrictions imposed by FIPS 186-3, the value of λ shall be at least twice the desired security strength (in bits) required for the digital signature. For example, if a security strength of 112 bits is required for digital signatures, a (truncated) message digest of (at least) 224 bits must be used. If required/desired, any approved hash functions except SHA-1 could be employed to generate (truncated) message digests of exactly 224 bits in length. (For SHA-224 and SHA-512/224, the hash function's output would not require truncation.) It is recommended that the hash function chosen should minimize the number of truncation operations required to achieve the required/desired length for the hash value. For the 224-bit example above, SHA-512/224 should be chosen over SHA-384 and SHA-512/256. All three hash functions employ one (internal) truncation operation to produce their output, but SHA-384 and SHA-512/256 would each require an additional (external) truncation operation to pare their output down to the desired length of 224 bits.

original_blocks.html: Let C denote the bit length of the internal hash value that is denoted H in FIPS 180-4. (This H is often called the “chaining value” in descriptions of Merkle–Damgård-style hash functions.) Note that C is not (necessarily) equal to L, the bit length of the hash function’s output (see, for example, SHA-384 or SHA-512/t for any t < 512, for which L < 512 = C). In all currently approved hash functions, L ≤ C (with L = C for SHA-1, SHA-256, and SHA-512). The effective security strength4 of the HMAC key is the minimum of the security strength of K and the value of 2C. That is, security strength = min(security strength of K, 2C). For example, if the security strength of K is 128 bits, and SHA-1 is used, then the effective security strength of the HMAC key is 128 bits, since for SHA-1, 2C= 320. Note that, in this example, even if the security strength of K is greater than 320 bits, the effective security strength of the key is limited to 320 bits (the value of 2C for SHA-1). In general, there is no benefit in generating K with more than 2C bits of security. In particular, it is not sensible to generate K with a bit length that exceeds the input block size of the approved L-bit hash function employed in the HMAC construction. Such a K is hashed, and the resulting L-bit value is used instead. Returning to the SHA-1 example, suppose that the key K has a bit length greater than 512 (the input block size for SHA-1). Instead of using K directly, HMAC replaces K by its 160-bit SHA-1 hash value, and so the effective security strength of that choice of K is no more than 160 bits.

original_blocks.html: The successful verification of a MacTag does not completely guarantee that the accompanying text is authentic; there is a slight chance that an adversary with no knowledge of the HMAC key, K, can present a (MacTag, text) pair that will pass the verification procedure. From the perspective of an adversary that does not know the HMAC key K (i.e., the adversary is not among the community of users that share the key), the assurance of authenticity provided by a MacTag depends on its length and on the number of failed MacTag verifications allowed by a system for each value of the HMAC key. Let 2<sup>t</sup> be the number of failed MacTag verifications allowed by a system for each value of the HMAC key. The MacTag length, λ, and the value of t need to be chosen to avoid an unacceptable probability of falsely accepting forged data. The likelihood of accepting forged data as authentic is (1/2)<sup>(λ - t)</sup>. For example, if λ is 32, and a system allows 2<sup>12</sup> failed MacTag verifications for any given value of the HMAC key, then the likelihood of accepting forged data is (1/2)<sup>20</sup>. In order to increase assurance of authenticity, either λ would need to be increased, or the number of allowed failed MacTag verifications for each value of the HMAC key would need to be decreased. To avoid having an unacceptable probability of falsely accepting forged data at any time, the value of the HMAC key must be changed to a new value before the number of failed MacTag authentications reaches the maximum allowed number (2<sup>t</sup>). For the example above, with λ= 32 and t = 20, the HMAC key must be changed before the number of failed MacTag verifications reaches 2<sup>12</sup>. The actual second preimage resistance strength for SHA-1, SHA -224, SHA-256 and SHA-512 is approximately (L – M), where L is the output block size of the hash function, and the message is 2<sup>M</sup> input blocks in length. For example, if a message that is 2<sup>33</sup> bits in length (i.e., a gigabyte long) is hashed by SHA-256 (whose input block size is 2<sup>9</sup> bits), the second preimage resistance strength is (L – M) = (256 – 24) = 232 bits (where L = 256, and M = log<sub>2</sub>(2<sup>33</sup>/2<sup>9</sup>) = (33 – 9) = 24).
